page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-2 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the c4n server family. It features 2 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) paired with 7.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 3.5 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, requiring external block storage for operating system and application data. It also does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without the performance variability associated with shared-core or burstable instances. While benchmark data is not available for this specific configuration, the hardware profile represents a balanced resource distribution suitable for entry-level workloads that require predictable compute performance. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the lack of bundled local storage and GPUs positions this instance as a lean, compute-focused resource where users only pay for the core virtualized compute and memory infrastructure.

Given its 2 vCPUs and 7.0 GB of RAM, the c4n-standard-2 is suited for lightweight applications, microservices, small-scale web serving, and development or testing environments. It is also appropriate for basic containerized workloads and utility tasks that do not demand high memory capacity or local disk I/O performance.
